storyTitle: Bexley Council Achieves £800k Savings Through Digital Transformation and Cybersecurity Upgrades
headline: Bexley saves £800k through cybersecurity upgrades
committee: Finance & Corporate Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee Bexley, 14 October 2026
keyPointsHeading: How does Bexley cut IT costs?

watchability.hookStyle: Immediate factual council decision and resident impact
watchability.localRelevance: Directly affects Bexley residents and council services

claims.statement: Bexley Council expects to save £800,000 in capital expenditure by shifting to a Zero Trust security framework.
claims.sourceQuote: This saving is primarily driven by the adoption of a new 'Zero Trust' network security model, which is expected to Reduce the requirement of circa 800k capital to meet cyber compliance .
claims.sourceDocument: Finance & Corporate Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee Bexley, 14 October 2026

claims.statement: An audit found council software was previously run without proper ownership or resilience plans.
claims.sourceQuote: The application audit revealed inconsistencies in application ownership, support and management arrangements , with many applications managed on a 'best endeavours' basis
claims.sourceDocument: Finance & Corporate Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee Bexley, 14 October 2026

claims.statement: The full £195,000 reserve for Microsoft E5 licensing will be exhausted within the current financial year.
claims.sourceQuote: The transition from E3 to E5 had a revenue reserve... of £0.195m to fund the transition from E5, in the P4 forecast it is estimated that the entirety of the reserve will be required to be drawn down this financial year.
claims.sourceDocument: Finance & Corporate Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee Bexley, 14 October 2026

takeawayCard.title: Zero Trust Cuts Cyber Risks
takeawayCard.subtitle: Cloud migration will lower long term operating costs.

keyPoints: Zero Trust security cuts circa £800,000 in capital spending for cyber compliance.
Switching to Microsoft E5 draws down a £0.195m reserve across this year.
Audits revealed legacy systems were managed on a risky best endeavours basis.
